definitions.gloss: former times; days of old; the past
definitions.explanation: A literary or formal word referring to times long past, often used when reflecting on how things used to be.

examples.japanese: {昔日|せきじつ}の{面影|おもかげ}はない。
examples.english: There is no trace of what it once was.

examples.japanese: {昔日|せきじつ}の{栄光|えいこう}を{偲|しの}ぶ。
examples.english: To look back fondly on past glories.

examples.japanese: この{城跡|しろあと}には{昔日|せきじつ}の{壮大|そうだい}さを{感|かん}じさせるものがある。
examples.english: These castle ruins evoke the grandeur of former times.

notes:
A literary, formal word used primarily in written Japanese. Almost always appears in set phrases like {昔日|せきじつ}の{面影|おもかげ} (trace of former days) or {昔日|せきじつ}の{栄光|えいこう} (past glory). Conveys a sense of nostalgia or reflection on how much has changed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昔日|せきじつ}の{面影|おもかげ}: traces of former days
- {昔日|せきじつ}の{栄光|えいこう}: past glory
- {昔日|せきじつ}を{偲|しの}ぶ: to reminisce about the past
- {昔日|せきじつ}の{姿|すがた}: the form it once had

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {昔|むかし}: long ago; the past — the everyday word for the past, used in conversation and stories
- {往時|おうじ}: former times — similarly literary, but emphasizes a specific past era
- {古|いにしえ}: ancient times — even more literary and poetic, referring to very distant history
